Let
\[
N=n-r.
\]
Since \(n\ge 2r+2\), we have \(N>r\).

A degree \(d\) monomial of \(B\) has the form \(x^ay^bz^c\) with
\[
a+b+c=nd.
\]
I claim that such a monomial lies in \(A_d\) exactly when
\[
\left\lfloor {a\over N}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor {b\over N}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor {c\over N}\right\rfloor\ge d. \tag{1}
\]

Indeed, a degree \(1\) generator of \(A\) is uniquely near one of the three vertices because two coordinates cannot both be \(\ge N=n-r\). A product of \(d\) generators therefore corresponds to choosing nonnegative integers \(p,q,s\) with \(p+q+s=d\), and then allowing at most \(r\) units to move away from each of the \(p\) \(x\)-vertex generators, each of the \(q\) \(y\)-vertex generators, and each of the \(s\) \(z\)-vertex generators. Thus \(x^ay^bz^c\in A_d\) iff there are \(p,q,s\ge0\), \(p+q+s=d\), such that
\[
a\ge pN,\qquad b\ge qN,\qquad c\ge sN,
\]
which is equivalent to (1).

Now a monomial \(x^ay^bz^c\in A_d\) lies in the conductor iff every larger Veronese monomial \(x^{a+\alpha}y^{b+\beta}z^{c+\gamma}\), where \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=ne\), lies in \(A_{d+e}\).

So we need understand when a Veronese monomial fails to lie in \(A\). Write
\[
u=\left\lfloor {a\over N}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor {b\over N}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor {c\over N}\right\rfloor .
\]
A degree \(D\) monomial is missing from \(A_D\) exactly when
\[
u\le D-1.
\]
Write the exponents as \(Nq_i+v_i\), with \(0\le v_i<N\). Then
\[
nD=Nu+(v_1+v_2+v_3).
\]
Put \(t=D-u\ge1\). Since each \(v_i\le N-1\),
\[
r u+nt=v_1+v_2+v_3\le 3N-3.
\]
For fixed \(u\), this is easiest to satisfy when \(t=1\), so the largest possible missing-floor sum \(u\) is
\[
u_{\max}=\left\lfloor {3N-3-n\over r}\right\rfloor
=\left\lfloor {2n-3r-3\over r}\right\rfloor .
\]

Hence every monomial of \(A_d\) with \(d\ge u_{\max}+1\) is in the conductor, because no bad larger Veronese monomial can dominate it. Conversely, when \(d=u_{\max}\), choose remainders \(v_1,v_2,v_3<N\) summing
\[
ru_{\max}+n\le 3N-3.
\]
This gives a missing monomial in degree \(u_{\max}+1\) dominating some monomial of \(A_{u_{\max}}\), so \(A_{u_{\max}}\) is not contained in the conductor.

Therefore the least such integer is
\[
\boxed{\left\lfloor {2n-3r-3\over r}\right\rfloor+1}.
\]
